correctness.rationale: Connected spanning masks in K_(2,n) with n+1+k edges have exactly k+1 doubled right columns and one chosen edge per remaining column: any isolated right column disconnects, and a doubled one connects the hubs. The signed sum over choices forces every opposed-sign column to be doubled; then the remaining elementary symmetric sign polynomial is the binary Krawtchouk K_(k+1-t)(j;n-t) with factor (-1)^t 2^(n-k-1) times product of agreeing signs. Counting character strata proves multiplicities and exact rank sum. K_0=1 at t=k+1 attains the smallest nonzero multiplier, and the zero character attains maximal binomial size; Fourier diagonalization gives sharp pseudoinverse norm. For k=1, K1 vanishes at odd n and K2=((n-2j)^2-n)/2 vanishes precisely at square n, yielding the stated two disjoint nullity corrections. Independently enumerated connected masks and complete integer Walsh transforms for all k at n=2..6, comparing every coefficient, rank and spectral bounds. Universal result follows from the signed symbolic derivation, not finite testing.
